title: watchtower-notes-avi-2026-04-05
content:
Quick watchtower log - shift notes and follow-ups

2026-04-05 AM shift summary (02:00-10:00 PDT)
- primary pages: intermittent increased tail latency for hosted-api route /v1/generate (alerts fired 02:17, 03:42, 06:08).
- severity: S3 (user impact intermittent, degraded p95, partial mitigations applied).
- paging cadence: 02:17 -> first responder Maya -> escalated to infra on-call Samir at 02:33.

Immediate mitigations applied
- rolled traffic from model-r1-8q -> model-r1-4q variant (traffic split 70/30) at 02:28 to reduce memory pressure.
- bump autoscaler min replicas + add short 5m headroom (temp) at 03:00.
- cleared large KV cache items (cache eviction script run) to free GPU memory 03:10.
- result: p95 improved from ~920ms -> ~420ms, but intermittent spikes remained.

Observations / hypothesis
- correlation with long-sequence requests spiking (noticed higher proportion of tokens >1024 around alerts).
- logs show increased transformer_attention kernel time on certain machines (hostnames: gpu-prod-12, gpu-prod-27).
- one host (gpu-prod-27) reported OOM event around 02:06 per node-exporter + dmesg. Not full reboot but memory thrashing.
- possible contributing factor: recent rollout of runtime change (PR #912) touched cache eviction heuristics; timing aligns (rolled 01:50).

Follow-ups / action items (owners + rough ETA)
- A1: Create post-incident ticket with timeline + attach logs (owner: Avi) - SRE-4782 created, add full HAR from 02:00-07:00. ETA: 2026-04-06 EOD.
- A2: Revert/rollback PR 912 on staging and run load test variant with long-seq synthetic traffic (owner: Samir) ETA: 2026-04-06 noon.
- A3: Add runbook step to proactively check for large-sequence traffic and trigger cache-priority eviction (owner: Maya) ETA: 2026-04-07.
- A4: Mark gpu-prod-27 for hardware health run and increase alert sensitivity for early OOM signs (owner: Infra oncall) ETA: 2026-04-06.
- A5: Update hosted-api route dashboard to show sequence length distribution (owner: Observability) ETA: 2026-04-09.

Runbook TODOs (quick items to edit in runbook-notes)
- Insert a blurb under "Memory/Cache Pressure" for when sequence length > 1024: suggested steps + thresholds.
- Add a one-click revert checklist for model variant traffic-splitting. Include the exact traffic-split CLI commands used during mitigation.
- Add script snippet used to evict large KV entries (copy from /ops/scripts/evict-kv.sh) and annotate risks.
- Tune alert annotation so alerted document includes top 5 hosts by kernel_time and last OOM message.

Commands & useful snippets run during shift
- kubectl -n hosted get pods -l app=model-serving -o wide | grep gpu-prod-27
- gcloud logging read 'resource.type="gke_cluster" AND jsonPayload.route="/v1/generate"' --limit 1000 --format json > /tmp/generate-02-07.json
- ./scripts/traffic-split.sh --route hosted-api --from model-r1-8q --to model-r1-4q --ratio 0.7
- sudo grep -i oom /var/log/kern.log | tail -n 50  (on gpu hosts via bastion)

Monitoring snapshot at 07:15 PDT
- p50: 85ms, p95: 420ms (during mitigation), error rate: 0.8% (gradual), CPU avg (problem hosts): 78%, GPU mem free median: 22%.

Open questions / things to verify
- Did PR 912 change the eviction window only or also the metric used to prioritize keys? (Samir to confirm with author).
- Are there customers sending large single-turn prompts that spiked at 02:00? Need to cross-check request IDs and CS reports.
- Any infra maintenance around 01:45-02:00 that coincided with kernel upgrades? Check CHANGELOG/infra-maintenance.

Quick personal notes (for handover)
- If issues recur on next watch, do not hesitate to pull all long-seq traffic into a separate throttled pool rather than split 70/30; this isolates memory characteristics.
- Reminder: add a short blurb in my personal runbook about the traffic-split script flags --wait-for-drain and --force-commit.

Potential follow-on work (nice-to-have)
- Build small synthetic generator to mimic 4-5 long-seq customer calls and run nightly against staging after any runtime change. (pref: run as GH action).
- Automated regression check: when a runtime PR lands, run a short memory-pressure smoke test targeting tile sizes and attention kernel timings.

End-of-shift handover to night SRE: Maya (on at 22:00 PDT)
- Key items to watch: p95 for /v1/generate, OOM events, increase in sequence-length>1024 requests.
- Slack channel: #sre-runtime-alerts, thread pinned with logs: https://redwoodworkspace.slack.com/archives/C04567ABC/p1712222222000

Notes saved in drive; will link to the ticket with artifacts.

-- Avi
